new_entities.name: Low-dose doxepin for insomnia
new_entities.description: Use of low-dose doxepin, typically 1 to 6 mg at bedtime, to improve sleep maintenance in chronic insomnia.

new_entities.name: Sleep maintenance
new_entities.description: The ability to remain asleep through the night without frequent awakenings.

edges.effect_quant: Across randomized placebo-controlled trials, low-dose doxepin consistently improves wake after sleep onset and late-night sleep continuity. The 2014 systematic review judged low-dose doxepin to have a small-to-medium effect on sleep maintenance and duration, while pivotal adult and elderly trials showed significant wake-after-sleep-onset reductions versus placebo over one to twelve weeks.
edges.population: adults and older adults with chronic primary insomnia, especially those whose main complaint is waking during the night or too early in the morning
edges.mechanism: At very low doses, doxepin acts mainly through potent H1 histamine receptor antagonism, decreasing nocturnal wakefulness without behaving like an antidepressant-dose tricyclic regimen.
edges.summary: This is a strong protective sleep-maintenance edge. The best evidence supports low-dose doxepin as a maintenance-focused insomnia therapy more than as a pure sleep-initiation drug.
edges.caveats: Benefits are strongest for staying asleep rather than falling asleep. Trial programs were largely industry-sponsored, and although next-day sedation was generally limited at these doses, individual tolerability still matters in older adults.

evidence.citation: YeungWF et al 2015 Sleep Med Rev
